decisions.question: e-8054

source.question: e-8054
source.value:
Let's make entries below $a_{11}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 5 & -7 \\ 4 & -2 & 4 & -5 \\ -3 & 3 & -3 & -4\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -1 & -9 \\ 0 & -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 0 & 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 & -9 \\ -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & -1 & -9 \\ -10 & -8 & -9 \\ 9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's make entries to the left and to the right of $a_{23}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -3 \\ 2 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ -4 & -4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & 2 & -2 \\ -1 & -10 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-8005

source.question: e-8005
source.value:
Using elementary column operations, let's make entries to the right of $a_{31}=1$ equal to zero.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (or column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & -3 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+3{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-3){C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 6 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ -3 & -5 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -3 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(11-3) \\  & =32.\end{aligned}
$$
